text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The head of the rightwing Christian Liberal Party Chamoun: "I did not meet Netanyahu (Israeli PM), I will not meet him and I will not leave Lebanon".
-Commenting on a detention campaign carried out by the government, President Hrawi said: We will not allow a few people to threaten internal stability.
-"Night visitors" (security forces) detained a journalist at an An-Nahar without any judicial mandate.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Sfeir says freedoms are suppressed in the country.
-Israel deported a Lebanese family from the south Lebanon occupation zone and shelled villages in the western and eastern sectors outside the zone.
-The weekly treasury bill issue of December 19 raised 428.3 billion Lebanese pounds, posting a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 219.5 billion pounds.
-The European Union grants Lebanon 25 million Ecu to plan public sector investment.
-Some 4,000 new traffic lights will spread across Beirut by 1997 spring.
-President Hrawi to visit Maronite Patriarch Sfeir tomorrow in Bkerki.
-Palestinians held a sit-in outside some clinics of the U.N. Relief and Work Agency for refugees in Sidon to protest against the organisation's new medical policies.
